mcat_description.short: Sintex Portable Toilets are prefabricated, ready-to-use sanitation cabin units manufactured or branded under the Sintex name, constructed from FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), PVC, or steel, and sold as complete self-contained toilet enclosures. They are supplied per piece or per unit block and are designed for quick installation without civil construction.
mcat_description.long: Sintex Portable Toilets are factory-built, modular sanitation enclosures made primarily from FRP or PVC, available in Indian squat-pan and Western commode configurations, and supplied as single-seater cabins, twin-seater units, or multi-cabin toilet blocks. Standard cabin dimensions range from 3×3×7 ft to 4×4×8.6 ft, with built-in overhead water tanks (typically 200–500 litres), ventilation points, and bulb-holder electrical provisions. The Sintex brand is the dominant trade reference in India for this product category, with the name used generically by buyers and sellers to describe FRP/PVC prefabricated portable toilet cabins regardless of the actual manufacturer. Key applications include construction site sanitation, public events, government rural sanitation schemes (Swachh Bharat Mission), industrial labour welfare, and temporary public infrastructure.

market_context: Sintex is the dominant brand name in India's prefabricated portable toilet market, and the term 'Sintex portable toilet' is used generically by buyers to describe FRP or PVC prefabricated sanitation cabins regardless of actual manufacturer — making this a brand-dominant MCAT where the brand name functions as a category descriptor. The market is served by a mix of genuine Sintex-authorised dealers and independent FRP/PVC cabin manufacturers who use the Sintex name as a quality benchmark or trade reference. Two primary material streams exist: FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic) — the dominant and higher-durability option — and PVC, which is lighter and lower-cost; steel/MS frame variants are a smaller segment. Toilet seat type (Indian squat pan vs Western commode) is the primary product differentiation axis for buyers, followed by cabin size and water tank capacity. The Sintex Nirmal Toilet Block (rotomoulded, compact format) is a distinct government-scheme-oriented sub-product used in Swachh Bharat Mission and rural sanitation programmes. The Sintex Sugam Toilet uses PUF insulated sandwich panels and is positioned for semi-permanent installations. Demand is concentrated in construction-heavy states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Delhi NCR, Karnataka) with Chennai emerging as a strong regional market based on keyword geography signals. Bio-toilet variants (with DRDO-based biodigester systems) are a growing sub-segment for highway and remote-location applications where sewage connection is unavailable.
